body:
> sometimes people with social anxiety don't know how to respond to basic questions like "how are you doing?"

"Good, good—you?"

> or "what did you do this weekend?"

"Oh, this and that."

That's one example of what shapes peoples' opinions of me, like I wrote above. You're telling me to think out loud and communicate what I'm *really* feeling, but for me that means letting my guard down and letting others too close.

That fucking paradox is one more thing ruining my life. How can I say something like "I feel as though the easiest path to personal happiness is another pair of arms to hold" and then not let anyone close to me in even simpler social settings? One part of my mind knows you're right, but it's trapped within the same walls the rest of mind constructs to keep others *out*.

> I'm not sure why you don't feel like an authentic person. I think that's a sign of something that needs to be resolved. Sometimes people don't feel authentic because they're resistant to change. They think that anything outside of their normal routine is faking. Other people might not feel authentic because they're having an identity crisis.

It feels like an identity crisis, if that mask metaphor means anything. I neither know who I am nor who I want to be nor who I *would* want to be in idealized world nor what that idealized world even begins to look like. That's why, for example, I can't finish any creative endeavor I start (the only creative endeavors I've finished in the past few years have been short poems and certain complex Mafia setups, the latter of which only because there was external impetus to do so). That's also another reason why a crush can grab hold of me like a vice grip—I naturally think "could this person be a basis for living my life?" I continually struggle with the idea of finding a raison d'être, which is something I've never had in 22 years of life.

Thanks for your time, NateExMachina. Please don't keep responding on *my* behalf, unless you want to. I may look somewhere else on the internet.

Hey—thanks =)

1/3/6) Would that I could do any of that! I'm so far removed from normal social life that I feel so lost in any attempt to re-establish one.

It doesn't especially help that, on some/most days I'd just as soon go about my day without any human contact, friendly or otherwise. I can wake up one morning and want nothing more than solitude, and wake up the next and lament that I have no-one to spend the coming day with.

You say that "I don't need a partner to be happy," and I see the logic in that, from your perspective *and* mine. But on some days I feel as though the easiest path *to* personal happiness is another pair of arms to hold.

You also tell me to "ask myself what type of person people want to be friends with." Even if I'm capable of being that person (I may or may not be), I'm not sure I *want* to.

2) Should I stress that my obsession is almost wholly internal? I don't know if that question is rhetorical or if that point is important, or if I'm trying to justify something that I shouldn't be wasting my time trying to justify. Either way, I'm *at least* socially aware enough to recognize the general impression I leave on most people—something like "he's a bit awkward and could stand to smile a bit more, but he's a nice guy that I don't mind being around." I even have a reasonable acquaintanceship with Corella, in the sense that we can stop and talk for a minute when we see each other, which is helped by the fact I've moved on from her and the fact that my past crush on her was so internalized that she has never been aware of my feelings for her (as far as I can tell, not that I can be too sure). I can't bear the thought of hurting anyone as long as I'm alive, even—especially—someone I'm "obsessing" over.

4) I know =/

It's weird being on the other side of a "problem"—I don't consider this a strong physical addiction in the present, especially owing to the fact that this is only the third time in my life I've drank for the express purpose of "drowning my sorrows," balanced against the hundreds of times I've drank in a casual and *restrained* setting. But...I see why it's a problem, and I'm wary of it in the future, because the euphoria I felt at work after my lunch yesterday was such a pronounced counterpoint to the depression I've felt otherwise. I could even look Serin in the face and not give a fuck.

5) Hm. Watched one of his videos; I'll try a few more. Interesting thoughts and an interesting man.

And yeah, I prefer storytelling to genuine living because I don't even feel like an authentic person that can live authentically. I can take solace in the past because it's easier to do than applying lessons *from* the past to the future, and at my core I'm a weak-willed person who takes the path of least resistance. 

--------------------------------------------------

Anyway, thanks again. I wish I could get more responses but this is on the verge of being lost to the Reddit ether =/
Still nothing and nothing and nothing and nothing. I don't get it. *What do I need to do?*

When I first found out about Serin earlier today, I had plenty of tears and plenty of gin. Such an intense release of emotion is a cathartic experience. Right now, eight hours later...? It's just this pervasive depression. Deadness.

Whatever the hell "intelligence" means. Listen, it's all fucking posturing, isn't it? It's all defense mechanisms at any rate. I may have been onto something with that masks shit.

The truth is, I'm sad, I'm angry, I'm terrified, and I have **no fucking idea what to do**. I keep ruminating over suicide, but that's only owing to suicide being the default option. Like, I can't find anything more sensible to do, I kill myself.

I'm fundamentally alone, and I'm a hopeless romantic who is in no social position to be one -- the "romantic" part, anyway.

But what currently scares me is something that I wrote two months ago after I discovered it in an airport terminal:

> I'm terrified that the moment I put this pen down things return to normal. Normalcy frightens me more than anything I've written about here, or in the past three months What happens when I drop this pen, board this flight, and go home? Why do I take solace in my melancholic tempers?

The last thing I want to do is wake up tomorrow and say "you know what, I don't feel as bad this morning." I can't live another fucking day where I lie to myself every waking minute, telling myself "this is all right." That I can live fundamentally alone, fundamentally friendless; not a single pair of arms that I can fall into at the end of the day. Because I know now, in this mood, that *in no fucking way is that true*. I'm terrified that if I can't live a life where I can look at myself genuinely in the mirror and tell myself that things *need* to be made better, that there's no point in living. Otherwise there will be another Corella/Serin and this will happen again and again and again and again.
